evidence: src/application/order-mapper.ts: toOrderDto(order: Order): OrderDto is the single Order→DTO mapping, used by advance-order-use-case.ts, cancel-order-use-case.ts, list-orders-use-case.ts (map(toOrderDto)) and place-order-use-case.ts
src/application/advance-order-use-case.ts and src/application/list-orders-use-case.ts both validate with the domain's isOrderStatus instead of their own status rules
src/application/place-order-use-case.ts (stock.reserve) and src/application/cancel-order-use-case.ts (stock.release) both go through StockAllocationService
src/application/get-stock-levels-use-case.ts: GetStockLevelsUseCase.execute maps products to StockLevelDto inline; no stock mapper exists, so nothing is bypassed
src/application/order-dto.ts declares StockLevelDto next to the order DTOs, a small naming inconsistency rather than a split in concerns

src/application/advance-order-use-case.ts and src/application/cancel-order-use-case.ts each repeat the findById + DomainError('NOT_FOUND') guard; this is use-case boilerplate, not a business invariant
parsedVerdict.reasoning: All files in src/application serve one concern: application use cases for order fulfilment and the stock reservations tied to it, plus the DTOs and the mapper that support them. Every order-returning use case (AdvanceOrderUseCase, CancelOrderUseCase, ListOrdersUseCase, PlaceOrderUseCase) converts its result through the single toOrderDto in order-mapper.ts, so there is one place for that mapping. Status validation goes through the domain's isOrderStatus rather than being reimplemented. Stock reservation and release go through StockAllocationService in PlaceOrderUseCase and CancelOrderUseCase. GetStockLevelsUseCase is a read-only query on inventory, which the order use cases reserve and release, so it is closely related rather than a separate concern. Some small points do not reach the fail threshold: (1) StockLevelDto is declared in order-dto.ts, a naming mismatch; (2) GetStockLevelsUseCase maps products inline, but no stock mapper exists for it to bypass; (3) the 'order not found → DomainError("NOT_FOUND")' guard is repeated in two use cases. That guard is ordinary use-case boilerplate, not a duplicated business invariant.
